author: Shri Raghavendra Swami
commentary: अयुक्तस्य भावना नेत्ययुक्तम् । कृतश्रवणमननस्य पुंसो ध्यानोपपत्तेरित्यत आह ॥ इन्द्रियाणामिति । चक्षुरादीन्द्रियाणां स्वैरं विषयेषु चरतां गच्छतामनु पृष्ठभावितया मनो विषयान्प्रति विधीयते ईश्वरेण क्रियते यत्तन्मनस इन्द्रियाणां पृष्ठभावितया ईश्वरेण करणं अस्य पुंसः प्रज्ञां परोक्षनिश्चयं हरति । उत्पत्स्यत्यपरोक्षज्ञानं निवारयति । उत्पन्नमपि ज्ञानं चित्तरिरोधहीनस्य न ध्यानोपयोगी सदपरोक्षज्ञानाय प्रभवतीत्यर्थः । कथम् । अम्भसि वायुर्नावमिव प्लवमिवेति ॥ २.६७॥
translation:
That the mind is made to follow the wandering senses sends his understanding adrift, even as the wind does the vessel upon the waters. (67)
V. The construction in this verse, natural as it may appear in Sanskrit, presents a peculiar difficulty to translation. But it is important to keep the construction in view, which is followed here. The sense is: The mind is naturally constituted (by the Lord with the tendency) to follow the lead of the senses. It is the constitution that allows the true conclusions of the Sâstras to slip easily from his mind; It even prevents the rising of such conclusive knowledge; and the little that may find place in it cannot in the absence of control be useful in promoting meditation and thereby obtaining for his direct perception. (67).
